scenes.text: Have you ever wondered how mapmakers protect their incredibly valuable work from sneaky plagiarists who want to steal their data?
Way back in the 1930s, two clever mapmakers created a fake town in upstate New York called Agloe, placing it secretly on a remote dirt road as a genius copyright trap.

When a massive rival company copied their map years later, the creators prepared to sue, but they shockingly discovered that a real, physical general store had actually been built at those exact coordinates.

The store owners named it the Agloe General Store simply because they saw it on that original map, literally bringing a fictional town to life, so follow for more mind-blowing history and comment below if you would ever visit a paper town!
